stories.headline: Iran hits US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain with drones and stops two tankers in Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Iran's army said on Friday, July 31, that it had struck US military assets at Kuwait's Ahmad al-Jaber air base with drones, targeting aircraft shelters, satellite communication systems and equipment warehouses
key_facts.excerpt: The Iranian army said on Friday that its forces had targeted strategic US military facilities at Kuwait's Ahmad Al-Jaber airbase in a drone attack... it had targeted hangars, satellite communication systems and equipment warehouses using drones.

key_facts.fact: Iran's army also said it attacked US facilities at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, targeting power generators, navigation systems and support buildings
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's army also claimed Thursday to have attacked U.S. facilities at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, targeting power generators, navigation systems and support buildings.

key_facts.fact: Kuwait's defence ministry said it detected hostile drones in Kuwaiti airspace from dawn on Friday and 'engaged and destroyed' them, blaming 'Iranian aggression'
key_facts.excerpt: Kuwait's defense ministry said that it had 'detected hostile drones inside Kuwaiti airspace since dawn today' and 'successfully intercepted and destroyed them.'

key_facts.fact: The IRGC said it struck and stopped two oil tankers that tried to cross the Strait of Hormuz under US military 'aerial escort', and that four other tankers turned back
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC said the 'non-compliant oil tankers … were struck and stopped, while four other oil tankers quickly changed course and returned to their previous locations.'

key_facts.fact: Iran said the attacks answered a US strike on a home on Qeshm Island; local media reported three members of one family were killed there
key_facts.excerpt: The Iranian army said the strikes came 'in response to the recent aggression by the terrorist US military against our country and its brutal attack on a residential home on Qeshm Island'. Local media reported yesterday that three members of a family were killed.

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM rejected the IRGC's claim that its missiles destroyed three US F-35s at Jordan's al-Azraq air base, saying 'No US aircraft were destroyed or damaged in recent attempted Iranian attacks'
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command (CENTCOM) posted on X, 'No US aircraft were destroyed or damaged in recent attempted Iranian attacks.'

key_facts.fact: Oil prices reversed early losses and traded higher on Friday morning after the tanker report, while mediator Pakistan said US-Iran talks continue, 'particularly on the Strait of Hormuz'
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices traded higher on Friday morning, reversing earlier losses, after Iran's Fars said the IRGC stopped two tankers from passing through the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Bank of Japan holds at 1% but warns inflation may overshoot, after Tokyo props up the yen

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Japan kept its short-term policy rate at 1% on July 31, in an 8-1 vote; board member Hajime Takata dissented, proposing a hike to 1.25%
key_facts.excerpt: BoJ keeps rates unchanged at 1.00%, as expected, through 8-1 vote... Takata dissented and proposed a 25bps hike, which was turned down by a majority vote.

key_facts.fact: The BOJ warned for the first time that underlying inflation could exceed its 2% target, signalling further rate hikes
key_facts.excerpt: The Bank of Japan kept interest rates steady on July 31 but warned for the first time that underlying inflation could exceed its target, signalling further rate hikes in the wake of the government's yen-buying intervention.

key_facts.fact: Japan's government conducted yen-buying, dollar-selling intervention in New York markets on July 30; the yen still hovered around 160.76 per dollar after the BOJ decision
key_facts.excerpt: The BOJ's decision and its hawkish statement pushed up the two-year Japanese government bond yield but did little to prop up the yen, which hovered around 160.760 per dollar... market intervention in New York markets on July 30, a move that failed to give the yen a sustained boost.

key_facts.fact: Governor Kazuo Ueda said the BOJ could 'accelerate the pace of rate hikes' if financial conditions are judged overly accommodative, flagging 'meaningful upside risks' to inflation
key_facts.excerpt: Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda on Friday said that if financial conditions are judged to be overly accommodative, BOJ could 'accelerate the pace of rate hikes'... warning of 'meaningful upside risks' to inflation due to rising wages and prices, as well as elevated oil prices and a weak yen.

key_facts.fact: The BOJ cut its core inflation forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 to 2.5% from 2.8% projected in April, while raising its fiscal 2027 forecast
key_facts.excerpt: In the outlook report, the BOJ revised down its core inflation forecast for the current fiscal year ending in March 2027 to 2.5% from 2.8% projected in April due to stabilising oil prices. But it revised up its forecast for fiscal 2027.

key_facts.fact: The BOJ added strong AI-linked demand and currency moves, alongside Middle East developments, to the factors it will weigh when timing further hikes; June's increase took the rate to a 31-year high
key_facts.excerpt: Ueda said that the recent weakening of the yen against the U.S. dollar will be among the 'important' factors, along with the Middle East situation and the increase in artificial intelligence-linked demand... after the bank kept its benchmark rate unchanged at 1.0 percent following an increase to a 31-year-high in June.

stories.headline: Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness dumps its stock book to Citadel after 67% July loss

key_facts.fact: Situational Awareness, the AI-focused hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, sold the bulk of its public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin's Citadel, two sources told Reuters on Thursday, July 30
key_facts.excerpt: Situational Awareness, an AI-focused hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, sold the bulk of its stock portfolio to Ken Griffin's Citadel after being battered by heavy losses in its tech holdings, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The fund was down around 67% so far in July, according to a letter it sent investors
key_facts.excerpt: The fund was down around 67% so far in July after incurring heavy losses on AI stocks, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing a source who saw a letter the firm sent to investors.

key_facts.fact: The fund had grown to as much as $45 billion at the start of July before the losses; it was hit by declines in AI infrastructure holdings such as SK Hynix and by short positions in software names such as Adobe moving against it
key_facts.excerpt: The fund grew to as big as $45 billion at the start of July before big losses took hold... Situational Awareness has sustained significant losses in recent weeks as its portfolio of AI infrastructure investments such as SK Hynix declined while short positions in software companies such as Adobe moved sharply against it.

key_facts.fact: Situational will keep a book of roughly $10 billion after the deal, including stocks and private investments; it did not sell its stake in Anthropic
key_facts.excerpt: They said Situational will hold a book of roughly $10 billion after the deal comprised of stocks as well as private investments in companies like Anthropic. Situational has not sold its stake in Anthropic, the sources said.

key_facts.fact: Prime brokers including Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Citigroup helped facilitate the deal, with Citadel taking the leverage-financed portion of the portfolio
key_facts.excerpt: A number of top Wall Street prime brokers, including Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Citigroup, helped facilitate the deal... As part of the deal, Citadel is picking up the portion of Situational's public portfolio that was financed by leverage from brokers.

key_facts.fact: The 25-year-old Aschenbrenner was forced to sell the majority of his public equity holdings to Citadel on Wednesday; the fund's public book included AI hardware positions such as Nebius and Sandisk
key_facts.excerpt: The 25-year-old founder of artificial-intelligence-focused investor Situational Awareness was forced to sell a majority of his public equity holdings to Ken Griffin's $71 billion hedge fund Citadel on Wednesday... which included large positions in AI hardware stocks such as Nebius and Sandisk.

stories.headline: New York sues Kalshi as illegal gambling; CFTC files emergency motion to block the state

key_facts.fact: New York Attorney General Letitia James and Governor Kathy Hochul announced on July 31 that the state sued KalshiEX for running an illegal, unlicensed gambling operation through its prediction market
key_facts.excerpt: New York Governor Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James today announced that New York has sued KalshiEX, LLC (Kalshi) for running an illegal gambling operation in New York through its prediction market platform.

key_facts.fact: The suit says Kalshi never obtained a New York State Gaming Commission license and exposed New Yorkers, including people under the legal gambling age of 21, to financial risk; it seeks an injunction, forfeiture of all gains, restitution and fines equal to three times those gains
key_facts.excerpt: OAG is asking the court to order Kalshi to forfeit all illegal gains, distribute restitution to consumers who were harmed, and pay fines equal to three times the gains the company made through its illegal actions.

key_facts.fact: Court filings put the requested compensatory damages at at least $36 billion, pending a full accounting, plus $100,000 for each offering
key_facts.excerpt: According to court filings, the requested compensatory damages could total at least $36 billion, pending a full accounting.

key_facts.fact: Less than an hour before the state filed, the CFTC filed an 'emergency' motion in Manhattan federal court to stop New York's enforcement, calling it 'overreach' that would irreparably harm the agency and the markets it regulates
key_facts.excerpt: Less than one hour before New York sued Kalshi, the CFTC filed an 'emergency' motion in Manhattan federal court to stop the state's enforcement activity, calling it 'overreach' that would irreparably harm the agency and markets it regulates.

key_facts.fact: The filings follow a Manhattan federal appeals court's rejection on Wednesday of Kalshi's bid to escape New York gambling law while it appeals Judge Analisa Torres's July 8 refusal to grant an injunction against the state
key_facts.excerpt: The CFTC filing followed Wednesday's rejection by the federal appeals court in Manhattan of Kalshi's request to avoid being subjected to New York's gambling laws, while it appeals U.S. District Judge Analisa Torres' refusal on July 8 to issue an injunction against the state.

key_facts.fact: James filed similar petitions in April against Coinbase Financial Markets and Gemini Titan, and 44 state attorneys general wrote to the CFTC on Monday arguing it has no right to regulate sports event contracts
key_facts.excerpt: 44 state attorneys General on Monday sent a letter to the CFTC, claiming that the commission has no right to regulate sports-related event contracts, as part of a public comment period for the agency's first draft of regulations on prediction markets.

key_facts.fact: Kalshi said it was disappointed, arguing New York cannot shut down a federally licensed financial exchange
key_facts.excerpt: Kalshi expressed disappointment with the decision by the state, saying that New York can't shut down a federally-licensed financial exchange.

stories.headline: Zelensky says Russia used a North Korean missile in strike that killed six, then sent 255 drones

key_facts.fact: Russia launched more than 70 missiles and about 280 drones at Ukraine overnight into Thursday, killing nine people, with Kyiv and the western Lviv region the main targets, Zelensky said
key_facts.excerpt: Russia launched more than 70 missiles and about 280 drones, Zelenskiy said in a statement. The capital Kyiv and the western region of Lviv on Ukraine's border with Poland were the main focus of the attack.

key_facts.fact: In his nightly address, Zelensky said preliminary data showed Russia used a North Korean missile for the first time in a long while in the strike on the village of Radushne, where six people including three children were killed
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskiy said of the attack on the village: 'In Radushne, the Russians used a missile from North Korea for the first time in a long time – that is what preliminary data shows.' ... marking the first time in nearly a year that Russia has used such a weapon from its ally.

key_facts.fact: The following night Russia launched 255 attack drones, including jet-powered Shahed variants and decoys; Ukraine's Air Force said 195 were shot down or suppressed while 22 struck targets at 14 locations
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces used 255 attack drones, including Shahed drones (including jet-powered variants), Gerbera, Italmas, and Parodiya decoy drones... air defenses had shot down or suppressed 195 enemy drones... 22 attack drones struck targets at 14 locations.

key_facts.fact: Russian attacks killed at least nine people and injured 48 across Ukraine in the 24 hours to July 31, with search-and-rescue still under way in Lviv and Radushne
key_facts.excerpt: Russian attacks killed at least nine people and injured 48 others across Ukraine over the past day, local authorities said on July 31... Search-and-rescue operations continued for a second consecutive day in the city of Lviv... and the village of Radushne.

key_facts.fact: Trump said he was 'not sure' he would let Ukraine build Patriot missiles, weeks after saying at the NATO summit in Ankara that 'we'll give them the right to make Patriots'
key_facts.excerpt: US president Donald Trump said he was 'not sure' he would let Ukraine build Patriot missiles, The Financial Times reported on Thursday... On 10 July at the Nato summit in Ankara, Turkey, Trump said: 'We'll give them the right to make Patriots.'

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's envoy to Washington, Olha Stefanishyna, said Kyiv needs anti-ballistic missiles now and that licensing local PAC-3 production could take from 12 months to five years
key_facts.excerpt: Olha Stefanishyna told reporters that Ukraine was in discussions with the Pentagon about a license to produce Patriot PAC-3 missiles itself, but that process could take 12 months to five years.

stories.headline: Counter-drone firm Space-Eyes, backed by Eric Trump, to go public via SPAC at $638M

key_facts.fact: Space-Eyes agreed to go public by merging with McKinley Acquisition Corp in a deal valuing the combined business at $638 million, according to four people familiar with the matter
key_facts.excerpt: Defence technology company Space-Eyes has agreed to go public through a merger with special purpose acquisition company McKinley Acquisition Corp, in a deal valuing the combined business at US$638-million, according to four people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Eric Trump recently became the third-largest private investor in Space-Eyes and will serve as a strategic adviser to the combined company
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump's son Eric Trump has recently become the third-largest private investor in the original Space-Eyes... Eric Trump will serve as a strategic adviser to the combined business following the transaction.

key_facts.fact: The Miami-based company builds AI-powered counter-drone and geospatial intelligence systems for governments and has generated about $1 million in annual revenue, operating mainly as an R&D company
key_facts.excerpt: which has operated primarily as a research-and-development company and generated about US$1-million in annual revenue... The Miami-based company develops artificial intelligence-powered counter-drone and geospatial intelligence technologies for governments and agencies.

key_facts.fact: The transaction is expected to provide up to $251.7 million in gross proceeds, including McKinley's trust account and a planned PIPE financing
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction is expected to provide up to US$251.7-million in gross proceeds, including capital held in McKinley's trust account and a planned private investment in public equity, or PIPE, financing.

key_facts.fact: The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the combined company trading on Nasdaq under the ticker 'CUAS', a reference to counter-unmanned aerial systems
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, with the combined company expected to trade on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol 'CUAS'.

stories.headline: Xi orders PLA to expand military use of unmanned and AI systems before its 99th anniversary

key_facts.fact: Xi Jinping called for enhancing the military application of unmanned intelligent technologies and advancing network information systems to gradually establish an 'intelligent military system'
key_facts.excerpt: He called for enhancing military application of unmanned intelligent technologies and advancing the development and application of the network information system to gradually establish an intelligent military system.

key_facts.fact: Xi made the remarks at a Politburo group study session on Thursday, ahead of the People's Liberation Army's 99th anniversary on Saturday, August 1
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking ahead of the PLA's 99th anniversary on Saturday, Xi said the military had made 'significant progress' in modernisation and called for 'decisive' advances... He told a Politburo group study session on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Xi said combat capability remains the ultimate objective and testing criterion of high-quality military modernization, and pressed for the PLA's 2027 centenary goals to be met on schedule
key_facts.excerpt: Combat capabilities remain the ultimate objective and testing criterion for promoting the high-quality modernization of national defense and the armed forces, Xi said.

key_facts.fact: He also urged deeper anti-corruption work and tighter oversight of major military projects, and called closer military-civilian industrial integration 'a necessary path' to a modern army
key_facts.excerpt: Xi also reiterated the importance of political indoctrination for the People's Liberation Army (PLA), urging efforts to advance the fight against corruption and improve oversight of major projects... Xi repeated the importance of closer integration between the military and civilian industries, calling it 'a necessary path' to building a modern army.

key_facts.fact: China aims to basically complete the modernization of its defence and armed forces by 2035 and build a 'world-class' military by 2049
key_facts.excerpt: China aims to basically achieve the modernisation of its national defence and armed forces by 2035 and build a 'world-class' military by 2049, the centenary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
